record.issuing_body: Minnesota Legislature (94th Legislature, 2026 session; chief author Rep. J. Hanson); signed by the Governor
record.summary: Bars whoever owns or controls a website, application, software, program or other service from letting users access, download or use it to 'nudify' an image or video, that is, to alter or generate it so that it realistically shows intimate parts of an identifiable person not shown in the original, or from nudifying images for users; advertising or promoting such services is banned. Services that need a user's own substantial technical or artistic skill are exempt. Depicted individuals may sue for up to three times actual damages, punitive damages and injunctive relief, and the Attorney General may seek civil penalties of up to USD 500,000 for each unlawful access, download or use.
record.notes: Passed the House 132-1 (23 Apr 2026) and the Senate 65-0 (29 Apr 2026); presented to the Governor on 6 May 2026 and signed on 7 May 2026; effective 1 Aug 2026 for causes of action accruing on or after that date. Civil penalties go to the general fund, and each year's balance is appropriated to the Office of Justice Programs for grants to organisations serving victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, child abuse and other crime. The section does not alter the liabilities and protections of 47 U.S.C. § 230. xAI challenges the law in federal court as a restriction of constitutionally protected free speech; US District Judge Donovan Frank refused to block it in September 2026, finding no showing of irreparable harm and undue delay, but on 2 Oct 2026 the US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit granted xAI an injunction that puts the law on hold while the lawsuit proceeds.
record.scope_note: The statute regulates services that alter or generate realistic intimate images of identifiable people and does not name artificial intelligence; included as Minnesota's operative instrument against deepfake 'nudification' tools.

changes.issuing_body: the stored files do not name the Governor; 'signed by Governor Tim Walz' becomes 'signed by the Governor'
changes.summary: the closing sentence ('targets providers of AI image-generation tools rather than individual users') is removed: the statute does not mention artificial intelligence; the definition of 'nudify' is spelled out instead
changes.notes: the xAI sentence ('Press reports describe ...; its outcome was not verified') replaced by the course of the litigation from the stored MPR News report: the district court's refusal in September 2026 and the Eighth Circuit's injunction of 2 Oct 2026; presentment date, use of civil penalties and the 47 U.S.C. § 230 clause added
changes.scope_note: added: the statute never names artificial intelligence, so it is in scope as a law that is not AI-specific but is the operative instrument for an AI-safety question (deepfakes), which AGENTS.md section 10 includes with a scope_note

judgment.status_reasoning: The session law shows 'Signed by the governor May 7, 2026' and its effective-date clause reads 'This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to causes of action accruing on or after that date.' 1 Aug 2026 is before 18 Oct 2026, so the section is in force. The stored MPR News report of 2 Oct 2026 says the Eighth Circuit 'put the law on hold for now, granting a request for an injunction by xAI'. An injunction pending appeal stops enforcement without repealing the statute or changing its effective date, and the status vocabulary has no value for an enjoined law, so 'In force' stands with the injunction in notes (as US-CO-01's notes describe a stipulated non-enforcement order); the open question asks a person to confirm this
judgment.scope_reasoning: The statute bans services that alter or generate realistic intimate images of identifiable people (deepfake nudification) and never uses the words 'artificial intelligence'. That is the AGENTS.md section 10 case of a law that is not AI-specific but is the operative instrument for an AI-safety question (deepfakes): in, with a scope_note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the Governor's signature, 7 May 2026; date_in_force is 1 Aug 2026 from the section's effective-date clause.

open_questions: Enforcement of section 325E.91 is on hold under the Eighth Circuit's injunction of 2 Oct 2026 in xAI's appeal (stored source: MPR News, secondary; no court order or official release is stored). The status vocabulary has no value for an enjoined law; this extraction keeps 'In force' and describes the injunction in notes. A person can decide whether an enjoined law should keep 'In force', and a later run should check the outcome of the appeal.
